content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any documents describing Level-1 hardware/deployability and allocated trigger-rate assumptions. Extract the three allowed candidate algorithms and note any documented hardware constraints or implementation limits relevant to each."},{"id":"s2","description":"For each candidate algorithm that is deployable in Level-1 hardware, run simulate_efficiency at thresholds 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, and 60 GeV. Record the returned signal efficiency for every algorithm-threshold point using record_results."},{"id":"s3","description":"Identify the algorithm-threshold regions with the highest recorded efficiencies. Around the best coarse threshold for each competitive candidate, run a finer threshold scan in 1 GeV steps, staying within 20 to 60 GeV and prioritizing thresholds near the apparent optimum. Record all fine-scan efficiencies."},{"id":"s4","description":"Compare all recorded efficiencies and select the deployable candidate algorithm and threshold with the highest signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate. If multiple settings have indistinguishable efficiency, prefer the lower threshold only if it remains within the allocated rate as confirmed by simulate_efficiency; otherwise prefer the simpler or more robust Level-1 implementation documented in the project materials."},{"id":"s5","description":"Prepare the final recommendation inputs for the reporting module: the chosen algorithm name, chosen threshold in GeV, its simulated signal efficiency at the allocated rate, and a concise numeric comparison to the next-best valid option."}]}
